title: The Factories Go Quiet
dialogue: The overnight reports confirm it. Seventeen factories across Kravenstal and Dravenhollow did not open this morning.
monologue: Marić warned me. He told me the grievances had been waiting. I told him growth would come before the waiting ran out. I was wrong about the timeline.

narrative.text: Wage floors indexed to inflation. Mandatory worker representation on privatized factory boards. A moratorium on foreign ownership transfers until a workers' protection framework is in place. These are not radical demands. These are the protections I told you they needed two years ago.
I did not organize this. I want that understood. The workers organized themselves. That is what happens when the government they voted for stops answering them.

Seventeen factories represents approximately nine percent of industrial output. If the strike holds for two weeks, the economic impact becomes material. If it spreads to the eastern provinces, it becomes a crisis.
The Halvekists are already framing this as proof that the free market agenda was reckless. They will be in front of every camera by afternoon.

strike_brief.monologue: He did not organize this. The workers organized themselves. That is what Marić said and the emphasis was deliberate — he is telling me the movement has momentum independent of him, which means he cannot stop it even if he wanted to. Which means I cannot manage this through Marić. I have to address the workers directly.

choices.text: Open direct negotiations with the strike organizers. Meet the core demands — wage indexing and worker representation. Not as a concession. As a correction.
Offer wage indexing only. Worker board representation requires Assembly approval — promise to introduce the legislation within sixty days.
Refuse to negotiate under strike conditions. The government does not set policy in response to industrial action. The factories reopen or the consequences escalate.
